# Test fixtures

Generated by `Rscript r/generate_all.R` from the repository root. Do not
edit by hand: this README is also generated. R is needed only to
regenerate; the Python tests read these files directly.

Generated with R 4.6.1, partykit 1.3-0, strucchange 1.6-0, sandwich 3.1-3, mlbench 2.1-11, jsonlite 2.0.0, MASS 7.3-66, nnet 7.3-21.

## Conventions

- Numbers are written with 17 significant digits in JSON and CSV, so every
  double round-trips exactly under a correctly rounded parser.
- `null` stands for R's `NA` or a non-finite value. In `split_search.objective`
  it marks an inadmissible candidate (R: `Inf`). In test p-values it marks a
  variable that was not tested (fewer than two distinct values in the node).
- Row indices (`rows`) and variable indices (`variable_index`, `test.best`) are
  0-based. Node ids, `kids`, `parent`, `fitted_node` and `partykit_varid` keep
  partykit's 1-based numbering.
- `estfun` is stored row-major: one inner array per row of the node, in
  `rows` order. Columns are named in `estfun_names`.
- In `control`, `"Inf"` is R's `Inf` and `null` is R's `NULL`.
- `stop_reason` is one of `split`, `minsize` (fewer than 2 * minsize
  observations), `maxdepth`, `test_failed` (the instability tests raised an
  error, caught by partykit's `try()`), `not_significant` (adjusted p-value
  above `alpha`), `no_admissible_split`, `pruned` (split found, then
  removed by post-pruning), or `no_estfun` (the fit function returned no
  scores, so partykit skipped the tests; only the extension models do this).
- `test.status` is `ok`, `not_run` (node stopped before testing, partykit
  stores no `test`), or `failed` (partykit stores `NA`).
- Factor responses (binomial) are encoded by `glm.fit` as 0 for the first
  level in `response_levels` and 1 otherwise.
- A dataset derived by deleting rows has `source_dataset` and `removed_rows`
  (0-based indices into the source data) in its schema, and the tree fixtures
  grown on it repeat both fields. Row indices in such a fixture refer to the
  reduced data.
- A fixture grown with `cluster` has a top-level `cluster` field naming the
  cluster column of its data CSV, and `n_clusters` in every node (the number of
  distinct cluster ids among the node's rows). Cluster ids are in the CSV, so
  a node's cluster vector is the cluster column at the node's `rows`.
- Each dataset has a `.schema.json` with column types, factor levels in R's
  order, the seed, the RNG kind and the generating code.
- Trees grown by `partykit::mob()` with an extension fit function have
  `function_name` `mob`, `fit_function`, `fit_args`, and per node a
  `model_info` object with the fit's extra outputs (for example `theta` for
  `negbinfit`, `separation` for `safelogitfit`, `classes_present` for
  `multinomfit`). See docs/extensions-spec.md for their meaning.

## Data

| File | Rows | Seed | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data/synth_diabetes.csv` | 768 | none (mlbench) | mlbench::SynthDiabetes, used by the partykit 1.3-0 mob vignette in place of PimaIndiansDiabetes. |
| `data/sim_gaussian.csv` | 600 | 20261001 | Simulated gaussian data with no, one and several planted splits. |
| `data/sim_gaussian_nonzero_w0.csv` | 543 | 20261001 | sim_gaussian without the rows where w0 is zero. Same columns, row order otherwise unchanged. |
| `data/sim_binomial.csv` | 800 | 20261002 | Simulated binary data with no, one and several planted splits. |
| `data/sim_poisson.csv` | 800 | 20261003 | Simulated count data with an exposure offset and planted splits. |
| `data/sim_cluster.csv` | 813 | 20261021 | Simulated grouped data: 30 schools, a school-level random intercept, school-level variables zs and zt, observation-level z1, z2, z3, and positive integer case weights w. The column school holds the cluster id. |
| `data/sim_cluster_few.csv` | 739 | 20261022 | Simulated grouped data: 21 ordinary schools and 3 large schools with high zs and different coefficients. The column school holds the cluster id. |
| `data/quine.csv` | 146 | none (MASS) | MASS::quine, days absent from school (Venables and Ripley). The thesis' negative binomial example (trusch.md:1339-1357). |
| `data/sim_negbin.csv` | 600 | 20261031 | Simulated overdispersed counts (theta = 2) with an exposure offset: no instability, a planted split at z1 = 0.5, a theta-only change, and a school-clustered version. Integer case weights w. |
| `data/sim_separation.csv` | 500 | 20261032 | Simulated binary data with a constant-response group (z2 = g4) and a region completely separated by x (z1 > 0.65); y_plain has no separation. |
| `data/sim_multinom.csv` | 900 | 20261033 | Simulated three-class responses (lo, mid, hi): no instability, a planted split at z1 = 0.5, and a school-clustered version. Weights w0 in 0 to 3. |
| `data/sim_multinom_noref.csv` | 600 | 20261034 | Simulated three-class responses (lo, mid, hi) where the reference class lo never occurs for z1 > 0.7. |
| `data/sim_cluster_models.csv` | 830 | 20261041 | Simulated grouped data for the cluster-robust leaf covariances: 36 schools of 8 to 40 pupils with school-level random intercepts, a planted split at z1 = 5, and responses for poisson (y_pois, offset log(exposure)), negative binomial (y_nb), multinomial (y_mn) and safe logit without separation (y_sl). The column school holds the cluster id. |

The glm.fit fixtures each have their own `data/glm_<case>.csv`, listed with
the fixture below.

## Tree fixtures

Generator: `r/fixtures/trees.R`. Each tree is grown twice, once by partykit
unchanged and once with an instrumented copy of `partykit:::mob_partynode`
that also records raw p-values, split-search objectives and the effective
`minsize` (see `r/fixtures/common.R`). The two trees must be identical or
generation stops.

Each file holds the full call, every `mob_control` setting, and per node: id,
parent, depth, kids, stop reason, rows, `nobs`, `minsize`, coefficients,
objective, the instability tests (statistic, raw p-value, log raw p-value,
adjusted p-value, trimming quantities), the split, every split candidate
with its objective, and `estfun`. `fitted_node` gives the terminal node of
each row. `decision_margins` reports how close the fixture is to an `alpha`
or split-objective tie.

### `trees/synth_diabetes_glmtree_binomial.json`

The mob vignette's glmtree example with default control settings.

Data `data/synth_diabetes.csv`. 2 inner and 3 terminal nodes.

```r
partykit::glmtree(formula = diabetes ~ glucose | pressure + triceps + insulin + mass + age, data = synth_diabetes, family = binomial(link = "logit"), epsilon = 1e-08, maxit = 25, alpha = 0.05, bonferroni = TRUE, minsize = NULL, maxdepth = Inf, mtry = Inf, trim = 0.1, breakties = FALSE, parm = NULL, dfsplit = TRUE, prune = NULL, restart = TRUE, verbose = FALSE, caseweights = TRUE, ytype = "vector", xtype = "matrix", terminal = c("estfun", "object"), inner = c("estfun", "object"), model = TRUE, numsplit = "left", catsplit = "binary", vcov = "opg", ordinal = "chisq", nrep = 10000, applyfun = NULL, cores = NULL)
```

## Extension tree fixtures

Generator: `r/fixtures/extensions.R` (specs) and `r/fixtures/trees.R`
(growing and extraction, as above). Same format as the tree fixtures, in
their own directory `extension_trees/` so that tests of the core models
can keep globbing `trees/`. The fit functions are in `r/extensions/`
and are specified in docs/extensions-spec.md. The generator also checks

## Reference-absent multinomial tree

Generator: `r/fixtures/extensions.R`. Extension tree format, in its own
directory `reference_absent_trees/` because some Python tests of
`extension_trees/` assume every multinomial node has scores (see
docs/sandwich-fixtures.md, section 3). The extra field `reference_absent`
has every root split-search candidate refitted side by side (classes
present, status and objective of each side, which add up to the
split-search objective) and the leaf without the reference class with its
objective.

### `reference_absent_trees/sim_multinom_noref_onesplit.json`

Multinomial logit where the reference class lo is absent for z1 > 0.7. Split-search candidates at or above the last lo observation have a right child without lo, fitted with mid as reference (objective only, no coefficients or scores). The tree splits there, and that leaf stops with stop_reason no_estfun (model_info status reference_absent). See reference_absent.

Data `data/sim_multinom_noref.csv`. 1 inner and 2 terminal nodes.

```r
partykit::mob(formula = y ~ x | z1 + z2 + z3, data = sim_multinom_noref, fit = multinomfit, maxit = 1000L, reltol = 1e-16, abstol = 1e-04, control = partykit::mob_control(alpha = 0.05, bonferroni = TRUE, minsize = 60L, maxdepth = Inf, mtry = Inf, trim = 0.1, breakties = FALSE, parm = NULL, dfsplit = TRUE, prune = NULL, restart = TRUE, verbose = FALSE, caseweights = TRUE, ytype = "vector", xtype = "matrix", terminal = c("estfun", "object"), inner = c("estfun", "object"), model = TRUE, numsplit = "left", catsplit = "binary", vcov = "opg", ordinal = "chisq", nrep = 10000, applyfun = NULL, cores = NULL))
```

## Cluster-robust covariance fixtures

Generator: `r/fixtures/sandwich.R`. One file per clustered tree, with every
leaf: `rows` (0-based), `n`, `k`, `n_clusters` (G), the tree's
coefficients, the refit used for sandwich (`refit_call`, evaluated with
`leaf` the data frame of the leaf's rows; its coefficients equal the tree's
and the difference is recorded), `vcov_model` (`stats::vcov` of the refit),
`bread` (`sandwich::bread`, n times the inverse Hessian), `hessian` (by
hand, see `hessian_definition`) and `vcovcl`: `sandwich::vcovCL` with
`type` HC0 and HC1 crossed with `cadjust` TRUE and FALSE, with the
school clusters and with `cluster = NULL` (each row its own cluster). Every
matrix is checked against the sandwich written by hand from the tree's
`estfun` (docs/api-design.md 5.1); the generator stops on a relative
difference above 1e-8. Matrices are row-major. All trees are unweighted.
docs/sandwich-fixtures.md records the decisions.

- `vcovcl/sim_cluster_lmtree_cluster.json`: sandwich::vcovCL on every leaf of trees/sim_cluster_lmtree_cluster.json. Model `lm`, 2 leaves, clusters per leaf 30, 30.
- `vcovcl/sim_cluster_glmtree_binomial_cluster.json`: sandwich::vcovCL on every leaf of trees/sim_cluster_glmtree_binomial_cluster.json. Model `glm_binomial`, 4 leaves, clusters per leaf 30, 25, 22, 30.
- `vcovcl/sim_cluster_few_lmtree_cluster.json`: sandwich::vcovCL on every leaf of trees/sim_cluster_few_lmtree_cluster.json. Model `lm`, 2 leaves, clusters per leaf 21, 3.
- `vcovcl/sim_cluster_models_glmtree_poisson_cluster.json`: sandwich::vcovCL on every leaf of cluster_trees/sim_cluster_models_glmtree_poisson_cluster.json. Model `glm_poisson`, 2 leaves, clusters per leaf 36, 36.
- `vcovcl/sim_cluster_models_negbin_cluster.json`: sandwich::vcovCL on every leaf of cluster_trees/sim_cluster_models_negbin_cluster.json. Model `negbin`, 2 leaves, clusters per leaf 36, 36.
- `vcovcl/sim_cluster_models_safelogit_cluster.json`: sandwich::vcovCL on every leaf of cluster_trees/sim_cluster_models_safelogit_cluster.json. Model `safelogit`, 2 leaves, clusters per leaf 36, 36.
- `vcovcl/sim_cluster_models_multinom_cluster.json`: sandwich::vcovCL on every leaf of cluster_trees/sim_cluster_models_multinom_cluster.json. Model `multinom`, 2 leaves, clusters per leaf 36, 36.

## predict fixtures

Generator: `r/fixtures/predict.R`. New rows for a tree fixture, each built
from the first training row of a node with some columns changed (`cases`:
`case`, `target_node`, `source_row`, `changed`, `note`): numeric splits at
the break, one step above it, at -Inf and Inf; ordered splits at the break
level, the level above and absent levels; nominal levels absent from the
node; the split variable missing; and per leaf the off-path partitioning
variables missing, the regressor missing, the offset variable missing and
the unchanged row. `newdata` holds the columns (factor labels; numbers with
null for NA and the strings "Inf" and "-Inf"). `routing` is
`deterministic` or `random` (partykit draws a kid at random for a missing
value, a level with no kid, or a value outside `.bincode`'s intervals such
as -Inf; `random_reason` says which), checked by predicting under 25 seeds.
`expected` has R's `node`, `response` and `link` for the deterministic
rows (null for random rows and for R's NA predictions). `failing_calls`
and `unseen_level_calls` record calls R stops on, with the message.

- `predict/sim_gaussian_lmtree_weights.json`: predict() of trees/sim_gaussian_lmtree_weights.json on new rows built from training rows: break values, absent levels, missing values on and off the path, a missing regressor. 93 rows, 20 routed at random.
- `predict/sim_binomial_glmtree_multisplit.json`: predict() of trees/sim_binomial_glmtree_multisplit.json on new rows built from training rows: break values, absent levels, missing values on and off the path, a missing regressor. 15 rows, 3 routed at random.
- `predict/sim_poisson_glmtree_multisplit.json`: predict() of trees/sim_poisson_glmtree_multisplit.json on new rows built from training rows: break values, absent levels, missing values on and off the path, a missing regressor and a missing offset. 20 rows, 3 routed at random.

## Node-level fit fixtures

Generator: `r/fixtures/extensions.R`. One fit of an extension model on a
subset of a dataset, with everything needed to repeat it: `rows` (0-based)
and `row_filter`, the design matrix `x` (row-major, columns `x_names`), `y`
(labels for factor responses, with `response_levels`), `weights`, `offset`,
`start` and `fit_args`. `result` holds the coefficients (null for NA),
`objfun`, `estfun` (null when the fit returns none) and `model_info`.

`checks` records the numerical verification of `estfun`, each enforced by
the generator: agreement with the analytic score written by hand
(`estfun_vs_analytic_max_rel`; exact for multinom, within the IRLS
tolerance for the glm.fit-based models, whose working weights lag one
iteration), with central finite differences of the per-observation
log-likelihood (`fd_vs_estfun_max_rel`, `fd_vs_analytic_max_rel`), and
column sums at the fit (`estfun_colsums`, relative to the column sums of
absolute values). `objfun_vs_loglik_abs` checks the objective against the
summed log-likelihood. For negbin, `theta_score_sum` is the theta score at
the returned theta (not part of `estfun`).

- `node_fits/negbin_quine_full.json`: All of quine, Days on Eth + Sex + Age + Lrn (7 coefficients). Data `data/quine.csv`, 146 rows.
- `node_fits/negbin_quine_eth_a_intercept.json`: Intercept only on the Eth = A rows (the thesis' node 2). Data `data/quine.csv`, 69 rows.
- `node_fits/negbin_sim_offset_weights.json`: y_one on x with offset log(exposure) and integer case weights w, rows with z1 <= 0.5. Data `data/sim_negbin.csv`, 279 rows.
- `node_fits/negbin_sim_start.json`: y_one on x with offset, starting values c(0, 0) as passed by split search with restart = FALSE. Data `data/sim_negbin.csv`, 600 rows.
- `node_fits/negbin_quine_deviance.json`: As negbin_quine_eth_a_intercept with objective = "deviance" (party 1.0-1's split criterion). Data `data/quine.csv`, 69 rows.
- `node_fits/safelogit_none.json`: No separation (z1 <= 0.65, z2 != g4). Must equal partykit's glmfit with binomial(). Data `data/sim_separation.csv`, 261 rows.
- `node_fits/safelogit_quasi.json`: Quasi-complete separation: regressors 1, x, d4 on z1 <= 0.65; every d4 = 1 row has y = 0, so the d4 coefficient diverges. Scores are returned. Data `data/sim_separation.csv`, 344 rows.
- `node_fits/safelogit_complete.json`: Complete separation by x (z1 > 0.65, z2 != g4). No estfun. Data `data/sim_separation.csv`, 115 rows.
- `node_fits/safelogit_constant.json`: Constant response y = 0 (z2 = g4). No estfun. Data `data/sim_separation.csv`, 124 rows.
- `node_fits/multinom_full.json`: All three classes, y_one on x, all rows. Data `data/sim_multinom.csv`, 900 rows.
- `node_fits/multinom_weights_zero.json`: Weights w0 with zeros: zero-weight rows are left out of the fit and get zero scores. Data `data/sim_multinom.csv`, 900 rows.
- `node_fits/multinom_start.json`: Starting values rep(0.1, 4) as passed by split search with restart = FALSE. Data `data/sim_multinom.csv`, 900 rows.
- `node_fits/multinom_absent_class.json`: Class hi absent (rows with y_one != hi and z1 <= 0.5): hi coefficients are NA and have no estfun columns. Data `data/sim_multinom.csv`, 322 rows.
- `node_fits/multinom_reference_absent.json`: Reference class lo absent: objective only, all coefficients NA, no estfun. Data `data/sim_multinom.csv`, 644 rows.
- `node_fits/multinom_single_class.json`: Only class mid present: objective 0, all coefficients NA, no estfun. Data `data/sim_multinom.csv`, 295 rows.

## Thesis cross-check

### `thesis_quine_crosscheck.json`

The quine tree printed in the thesis (grown with party 1.0-1) against
`extension_trees/quine_negbin_intercept_deviance.json`. Split variables, node sizes,
intercepts, theta, test statistics and 1 - p agree at the printed
precision; the generator stops otherwise. party 1.0-1 does not compile on
R 4.6 (its C code uses the `Calloc` macro, which R removed), so the thesis
printout is the reference.

## glm.fit fixtures

Generator: `r/fixtures/glm.R`. Each file records `glm.fit`'s coefficients,
deviance, null deviance, AIC, iteration count, convergence and boundary
flags, rank, fitted values, linear predictors, working weights and residuals,
and warnings. It also records partykit's `glmfit` objective and scores
(and `lmfit` for gaussian cases) on the same data.

### `glm/glm_gaussian_identity.json`

Gaussian, identity link, two regressors.

Data `data/glm_gaussian_identity.csv`, seed 20261011. Converged: TRUE, iterations: 2.

```r
stats::glm.fit(x = as.matrix(d[, c("x0", "x1", "x2")]), y = d$y, weights = NULL, start = NULL, offset = NULL, family = gaussian(link = "identity"), control = stats::glm.control(epsilon = 1e-08, maxit = 25L))
```

### `glm/glm_gaussian_weighted.json`

Gaussian with non-integer prior weights.

Data `data/glm_gaussian_weighted.csv`, seed 20261012. Converged: TRUE, iterations: 2.

```r

```

## p-value fixture

### `pvalues.json`

Generator: `r/fixtures/pvalues.R`. supLM log p-values from partykit's
`logp.supLM`, taken unchanged from inside `partykit:::mob_partynode`, over
336 combinations of trimming and k, each at 22 statistics.
Also chi-squared log p-values for factor tests, the Bonferroni/Sidak
adjustment on a few p-value vectors, and the Hansen table itself.

```r
logp.supLM(statistic, k, lambda) extracted from partykit:::mob_partynode; lambda from (nobs, trim, minsize) as in mob_grow_fluctests
```
